{"id":"JMAP-0x0q.45","title":"Sign peer blob fetches; classify failures","description":"Oracle: jmap-chat-spec 6bcd9d8 (quoted text). Mapped by wf_6712c4f8-c2b.

[chat-ext] Sign blob fetches; classify fetch failures; serve with grant check
Spec (2ad2d10, 95c24cb): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md L197: "A server MUST sign every HTTP request it sends to a peer to obtain a peer-role session, to invoke a Peer/* method, or to fetch a blob from a `fetchUrl` ({{blob-fetch}})"; L268: "The serving server, the one that issued the `fetchUrl`, MUST verify the signature as for any peer request. It SHOULD serve the blob only to a peer domain to which it has sent a payload carrying that `fetchUrl`, recording the grant before it sends the payload ... It SHOULD answer a verified request from any other peer domain with HTTP status 404"; L270: "The serving server MUST NOT redirect a blob fetch to another origin ... a fetching server does not follow such a redirect"; L432-435: "The connection fails, the request times out, or the serving server answers with a 5xx status: reject with `serverFail` ... status 429 ...: reject with `rateLimited`. ... status 403 or 404: reject with `invalidArguments`. ... The byte count or the `sha256` does not match: reject with `invalidArguments`."
Code: crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/deliver.rs:124-139 FederationBackend::fetch_attachment contract (no signing requirement, no status-to-error mapping; Err(e) is always serverFail); crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/deliver.rs:1150-1163 (step 11); crate-jmap-peer-auth-io/src/fetch.rs:24,35-40 Fetch/HttpsFetcher: unsigned GET only, follows up to 10 redirects; crate-jmap-peer-auth/src/signature.rs:170 sign() (usable for a body-less GET); crate-jmap-peer-auth-io/src/lib.rs:116 authenticate() (usable by a blob-serving endpoint)
Now: The library leaves the fetch entirely to the backend and documents only SSRF. Nothing tells the implementer to sign, map 5xx/timeout to serverFail, 429 to rateLimited, or 403/404 to invalidArguments. A conformant serving server rejects unsigned fetches, which turns transient failures into permanent message loss. No outbound code mints fetchUrls or records grants, and no blob-serving verification exists.
Change: Rewrite the fetch_attachment contract, and the new avatar fetch hook, to require a signed GET (tag jmap-chat-peer, covering @method and @target-uri, no content-digest) that does not follow cross-origin redirects. Spell out the L432-435 error mapping. Optionally add a signed blob-GET helper in peer-auth-io beside HttpsFetcher, with redirects disabled.
